text.p: These are the leading stories in the Kenyan press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- A motive for the murder of prominent criminal defence lawyer Samuel Ndungi is sought by police.
- A motion to give women one-third of all seats in Parliament is voted out by the house.
- Legal experts warn of chaos if the government does not allow for constitutional reforms to allow for free and fair elections this year.
- Edwin Osir is re-elected unopposed as chairman of the Kisumu branch of the ruling party.

- The Forum of Coffee Millers accuses the Coffee Board of Kenya of not publishing its annual financial report for the past five years and says the board cannot account for 10 billion shillings deducted from farmers in that time.
- Kenya ratifies the United Nations Chemical Weapons Convention.
- A British political lobby group is linked to the opposition to pressurise for constitutional reforms before the next general elections.
- The National Executive of opposition Kenya National Congress party suspends its chairman Chibule wa Tsuma.
